paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : TriviaQA confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy for multiple accuracy metrics across a range of initial confidence levels. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” represents a linear scale from 0.73 to 1.00, with tick labels every 0.05 units. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.71 to 1.00, with tick intervals of 0.05. The first line, plotted in blue with solid markers and a line style, begins at a value of approximately 0.82 at an initial confidence of 0.80 and steadily decreases to approximately 0.78 at 1.00. The second line, represented by orange diamonds and a dashed line style, starts at a value of approximately 0.72 at an initial confidence of 0.79 and decreases to approximately 0.17 at 1.00. The third line, depicted as green triangles and a dashed line style, begins at a value of approximately 0.75 at an initial confidence of 0.73 and then increases to approximately 0.93 at 1.00. Finally, the fourth line, shown as teal squares and a dashed line style, starts at a value of approximately 0.79 at an initial confidence of 0.82 and decreases to approximately 0.80 at 1.00.
